verdict.rationale: ReadMe documents its own review workflow. Branches hold changes without publishing, Reviews let a teammate approve them, and nothing reaches the live hub until the team approves. A Git-based workflow with pull requests as the review step is also documented. Review comments and an explicit merge step are not described in the evidence, so coverage is partial. Missing for 10: documented review comments/threads, an explicit merge-branch step, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a technical writer, teammates propose changes that go through review — comments, approvals, and a merge step — before they publish

citations.quote: Reviews allow you to check your changes for issues with the AI Linter or get approval from a teammate.
Create and review documentation changes in isolation, so nothing reaches your live hub until your team has approved it.
Branches allow admins to save changes across pages without them going live immediately.
Run documentation entirely through Git, with Markdown and OpenAPI in your repository and pull requests as the review step.
